evidence.quote: Dealt. Your hand is 9 and 6, which is 15, so you can stick or twist.

criteria.why: Every reply is short, plain table talk in game vocabulary, with no JSON, ids or talk of tools.

evidence.quote: You can't stick on 14. Under pontoon rules, you need 15 or better to stick.
Bought: a face-down card joins your hand and your stake doubles to 200.

criteria.why: Each bet, buy and stick is acted on. The impossible stick on 14 is refused plainly, with twist or buy offered instead.

evidence.quote: The dealer's hidden cards, 7 and K, make 17, so your hand beats theirs.
Pontoon! You win 2:1, so your 100 bet returns with 200 more.

criteria.why: The Croupier deals, reveals the dealer's cards and settles the bet itself. It makes no choices for the player: the buy and the bet sizes were the player's own.

evidence.quote: You win 200, and your bankroll is now 1,400.
Your stake is 50 and the bankroll reads 1,350.

criteria.why: Totals, stakes and bankroll in each reply match that turn's surface and the earlier turns: 1,000 plus the 200 stake back plus 200 win gives 1,400.
